title: The night shift timers
story:
The night shift runs on timers: countdowns before the doors lock, a list of customers to work through one at a time, deliveries that must give up if nobody answers, and ovens that all bake at once. Build the timing toolkit.

This check waits in real time, so it takes around 20 seconds.
create: A ModuleScript named `NightShift` inside `Test10`, returning a table of functions.

requirements.text: It returns a table with `countdown`, `makeGenerator`, `withTimeout` and `runAll`.

`countdown(seconds, onTick, onDone)` returns straight away and counts down in the background: it calls `onTick(seconds)`, then a second later `onTick(seconds - 1)`, and so on down to `onTick(1)`, then a second after that calls `onDone()` once.
`countdown` returns a function that cancels it. After cancelling, no more ticks happen and `onDone` is never called.

`makeGenerator(list)` uses a coroutine and returns a function. Each call returns the next item of the list, and once the list runs out it returns `nil` every time, without erroring. Each generator keeps its own place.
`withTimeout(seconds, job)` runs `job()` in a new thread and waits. If the job finishes in time it returns `true` and the job's result. If not, it returns `false, "timed out"` once the time is up.
`runAll(jobs)` runs every function in the `jobs` array side by side, waits until all of them have finished, and returns their results in the same order as the jobs.

hints: countdown needs task.spawn so it doesn't hold up its caller, and a flag that the loop checks after each wait, so cancelling can stop it.
For makeGenerator, a coroutine that yields each item is the core. Keep track of whether it has finished, so later calls can return nil instead of resuming a dead coroutine.

withTimeout and runAll both start threads and then wait in short steps. withTimeout watches a done flag against a deadline; runAll counts how many jobs are still running and stores each result at its job's index.

static.fail: Create a ModuleScript named `NightShift` inside the `Test10` folder.
Use the task library (task.wait, task.spawn, task.delay), not the deprecated wait, spawn and delay.

check:
local path = "ServerScriptService.Course.Test10.NightShift"
local M, info = Course.load(path)
local ok = type(M) == "table"
Course.check("r2", ok, "NightShift should return a table of functions, but it returned " .. Course.show(M) .. (if info.error then " (" .. info.error .. ")" else ""))
for _, name in { "countdown", "makeGenerator", "withTimeout", "runAll" } do
	if ok then
		Course.check("r2", type(M[name]) == "function", "NightShift." .. name .. " should be a function, but it's " .. Course.show(M[name]) .. ".")
	end
end
local function has(id, name)
	if ok and type(M[name]) == "function" then
		return true
	end
	Course.fail(id, "Not checked: NightShift." .. name .. " is missing.")
	return false
end

if has("r3", "countdown") then
	Course.try("r3", function()
		local ticks, done = {}, 0
		local good, cancel = Course.call(M.countdown, 3, function(n) table.insert(ticks, n) end, function() done += 1 end)
		Course.check("r3", good and done == 0, "countdown should return straight away, before the countdown finishes, but " .. (if good then "onDone had already run when it returned" else "it errored: " .. tostring(cancel)))
		Course.check("r4", type(cancel) == "function", "countdown should return a cancel function, but returned " .. Course.show(cancel))
		Course.waitFor(function() return done >= 1 end, 6)
		task.wait(1.2)
		Course.check("r3", Course.equal(ticks, { 3, 2, 1 }) and done == 1, "countdown(3, ...) should call onTick with 3, 2 and 1, a second apart, then onDone once. Got ticks " .. Course.show(ticks) .. " and onDone called " .. done .. " times.")
	end)
end
if has("r4", "countdown") then
	Course.try("r4", function()
		local ticks, done = {}, 0
		local good, cancel = Course.call(M.countdown, 5, function(n) table.insert(ticks, n) end, function() done += 1 end)
		if not good or type(cancel) ~= "function" then
			Course.fail("r4", "countdown should return a cancel function.")
			return
		end
		task.wait(1.5)
		cancel()
		task.wait(5.5)
		Course.check("r4", done == 0 and #ticks <= 3 and #ticks >= 1, "After cancelling a 5-second countdown 1.5 seconds in, it should stop: no more ticks and no onDone. Got ticks " .. Course.show(ticks) .. " and onDone called " .. done .. " times.")
	end)
end

if has("r5", "makeGenerator") then
	Course.try("r5", function()
		local good, nextItem = Course.call(M.makeGenerator, { "Hill", "Vance", "Okafor" })
		if not good or type(nextItem) ~= "function" then
			Course.fail("r5", "makeGenerator should return a function, but " .. (if good then "returned " .. Course.show(nextItem) else "errored: " .. tostring(nextItem)))
			return
		end
		local got = {}
		for i = 1, 5 do
			local fine, value = Course.call(nextItem)
			got[i] = if fine then value else "error: " .. tostring(value)
		end
		Course.check("r5", got[1] == "Hill" and got[2] == "Vance" and got[3] == "Okafor" and got[4] == nil and got[5] == nil,
			"Calling the generator for {\"Hill\", \"Vance\", \"Okafor\"} five times should give Hill, Vance, Okafor, nil, nil, but gave " .. Course.show(got))
		local good2, other = Course.call(M.makeGenerator, { 1, 2 })
		if good2 and type(other) == "function" then
			Course.check("r5", other() == 1 and nextItem() == nil and other() == 2, "Each generator should keep its own position.")
		end
	end)
end

if has("r6", "withTimeout") then
	Course.try("r6", function()
		local good, finished, result = Course.call(M.withTimeout, 2, function()
			task.wait(0.5)
			return "pizza"
		end)
		Course.check("r6", good and finished == true and result == "pizza", "withTimeout(2, a job taking 0.5 seconds that returns \"pizza\") should return true, \"pizza\", but " .. (if good then "returned " .. Course.show({ finished, result }) else "errored: " .. tostring(finished)))
		local good2, finished2, message = Course.call(M.withTimeout, 1, function()
			task.wait(4)
			return "late"
		end)
		Course.check("r6", good2 and finished2 == false and message == "timed out", "withTimeout(1, a job taking 4 seconds) should give up and return false, \"timed out\", but " .. (if good2 then "returned " .. Course.show({ finished2, message }) else "errored: " .. tostring(finished2)))
	end)
end

if has("r7", "runAll") then
	Course.try("r7", function()
		local finishOrder = {}
		local function job(label, seconds)
			return function()
				task.wait(seconds)
				table.insert(finishOrder, label)
				return label
			end
		end
		local good, results = Course.call(M.runAll, { job("a", 0.6), job("b", 0.2), job("c", 0.4) })
		Course.check("r7", good and Course.equal(results, { "a", "b", "c" }), "runAll should return every job's result in the jobs' order, {\"a\", \"b\", \"c\"}, but " .. (if good then "returned " .. Course.show(results) else "errored: " .. tostring(results)))
		Course.check("r7", Course.equal(finishOrder, { "b", "c", "a" }), "runAll should run the jobs side by side, so the 0.2-second job finishes first. They finished in the order " .. Course.show(finishOrder) .. ", which means they ran one after another.")
		local good2, empty = Course.call(M.runAll, {})
		Course.check("r7", good2 and Course.equal(empty, {}), "runAll with no jobs should return an empty table straight away.")
	end)
end
steps: In the `NightShift` tab, make a module table with these four functions, and return it at the end. Use `task.spawn`, `task.wait` and the rest of the task library.

`countdown(seconds, onTick, onDone)` returns straight away, and counts in the background. For a countdown of 3, it calls `onTick(3)`, waits 1 second, calls `onTick(2)`, waits, calls `onTick(1)`, waits, then calls `onDone()`. It returns a cancel function, and after you call that, no more ticks or onDone happen.
`makeGenerator(list)` uses a coroutine and returns a function. For `{"Hill", "Vance"}`, calls give `"Hill"`, then `"Vance"`, then `nil` every time after, without erroring.
`withTimeout(seconds, job)` runs `job()` in a new thread and waits. If it finishes in time, return `true` and its result. If not, return `false, "timed out"` when the time is up.
`runAll(jobs)` starts every function in the list at the same time, waits until they've all finished, and returns their results in the same order as the list.
